findings.finding: The construction program is the Solver node's decoding column group s1..s4 + the twin aa + the delivering lock LAST (phase-native-module-v1-c7, 1 Perception + 6 Solver contacts per row), compiled by the real module compiler. It is chosen over the Perception-level sampling column because the sampler, the trace writer and the credit tooling key scores and delivered contacts by arm label s1..s4, which a sampling column (arms of draws) does not give. The alternative (n = 5, c10) is implemented as an option (tfrl_v2_port_derive_cells.construction_block) and tested, not registered.
findings.remedy: none; the owner confirms or redirects (O-construction-group).

findings.finding: The plan's iteration-1 trajectories differ by decoding seed only; the Solver decoding group refuses a seed override and two equal overrides, so s1..s4 share the lock seed and differ in top_p (0.80 / 0.90 / 0.95 / 1.00) at temperature 0.7, top_k 20.
findings.remedy: a per-arm seed offset in the Solver decoding group would restore seed-only (rails_pending).

findings.remedy: fix the entity rule and register the policy (O-commit-policy).

findings.finding: slurp_module_construction.check_cell accepts the r01c variant only for vectors under vectors/slurp-stage3-construction-r01c-v1/ and the historical R01C agreement pin, which the port names do not satisfy. The construction cells therefore pin the minus-r01 train-exemplars twins directly (the committed VAR-2 R01C precedent) and do not name construction_roster.

findings.finding: T's supply bound is A's bound minus 8 and both caps (2,000 + 400 tokens) are folded into the frame's base prompt tokens. Default: 47 items, 15,768 estimated tokens against a limit of 17,406 (fits). Budget switch 6,144 / 7,168: 43 items, 14,828 against 14,334 (does not fit); the largest fitting bound is 40. The writer refuses under the switch.

The config loader (rails.native_episode_config) checks EVERY declared consumption_module block with verify_declared_module. Lock v2.2 carries the historical 268-B store pins, so a cell that pins the port's re-authored stores differs from what its block compiles to at ten leaves (docs/results/2026-10-30-badcase-verify-declared-module-l338-port.md). T never calls apply_to (it moves only the compiler's policy and role leaves, as the L338 port derive does), so the derive cannot hide such a clash from the loader.
findings.remedy: Resolved in the T lock switch (plan 3.14 addendum, plan section 13 ruling 3 (c)): the two Fold B cells declare lock v2.2-npu-port (v2.2 + the ten port store-pin leaves); the three construction cells pin the minus-R01 train-exemplars pool and declare lock v2.2-npu-port-r01c (v2.2-npu-port + exactly four train-exemplars release / snapshot leaves, read from the minus-R01 build receipt). The derive runs module_self_check before it writes and identities() runs verify_composed_module on every composed T cell, so a lock clash stops the writer; the loader accepts all five cells.
